description: TikTok Shop violations age out on a rolling 180-day Account Health Rating window. Here are the timelines, both appeal deadlines, and how to keep GMV growing.
dek: The point deduction and the enforcement action run on two different clocks, and most advice online only describes one of them. Here is what TikTok Shop's own Seller Center documentation says about the 180-day window, the 30-day and 15-day appeal deadlines, and what actually keeps GMV moving while a case is open.

llms_summary: TikTok Shop violations run on two separate clocks: the Account Health Rating point deduction ages out of a rolling 180-day seller window, while the enforcement action itself (pulled listing, blocked campaign, suspended ad account) clears only on its stated duration or a successful appeal. Sellers start at 200 points on a 0-1,000 scale; milestones at 150, 100 and 50 trigger 7, 14 and 28-day restrictions on new listings and mega-campaign enrollment, and 0 can mean permanent deactivation. A first appeal is due within 30 calendar days of the violation notice and a second within 15 calendar days of that decision, with two appeals maximum, filed at Seller Center > Shop Health > Violation Records. The widely quoted 90-day figure is the violation view for linked creator accounts, not seller AHR. Points are regained at 4 per 200 finished orders (capped at 20/week) and by passing the policy quiz tagged to the violation. Verified against TikTok Shop Seller Center documentation including the August 17, 2026 AHR update.
